museo-galileo:2427.name: Galileo Galilei
museo-galileo:2427.detail: The Museo Galileo gives his 1,273 mm telescope its own figures of 14× and 15 arcminutes. The player checks both a view’s detail and the area it covers.

museo-galileo:2428.name: Galileo Galilei
museo-galileo:2428.detail: The original eyepiece was lost. The museum gives the current telescope’s stated optical properties with a later replacement eyepiece.

umu:um-1.name: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
umu:um-1.detail: The museum identifies this brass instrument as possibly a later model around 1700. The bench uses a manufactured line plate so the range of earlier observations stays open.

umu:um-1.name: Tiemen Cocquyt
umu:um-1.detail: The study identifies UM-1 in its Figure 1 caption and records the preserved instrument’s 266× magnification.

us-navy:project-nekton-trieste-1960.name: Jacques Piccard
us-navy:project-nekton-trieste-1960.role: Participant in the 1960 Challenger Deep dive
us-navy:project-nekton-trieste-1960.detail: The Navy records Piccard reaching Challenger Deep aboard this specific Trieste on 23 January 1960.

us-navy:project-nekton-trieste-1960.name: Don Walsh
us-navy:project-nekton-trieste-1960.role: U.S. Navy lieutenant and participant in the dive
us-navy:project-nekton-trieste-1960.detail: The Navy dates Walsh’s Project Nekton dive in the vessel. The dated journey and the view from the vessel have different sources.

nhhc:nh-95258.name: Don Walsh
nhhc:nh-95258.detail: Walsh’s 1960 trip has its own record. The related profile was drawn in the early 1980s and shows the configuration of about 1963.

nasm:a19700102000.name: Michael Collins
nasm:a19700102000.detail: Collins remained aboard Columbia in lunar orbit while Eagle took the other two crew members to the surface.

nasm:a19700102000.name: Neil Armstrong
nasm:a19700102000.detail: Armstrong travelled with the mission crew in Columbia and descended to the lunar surface with Aldrin in Eagle.

nasm:a19700102000.name: Buzz Aldrin
nasm:a19700102000.detail: Aldrin travelled in Columbia on the mission and descended with Armstrong in the separate Eagle spacecraft.

nms:t.1890.330.name: Diya’ ad-Din Muhammad
nms:t.1890.330.detail: National Museums Scotland records brass with silver star positions on the celestial globe he made in 1663. In the bench trial the player keeps a silver reference mark fixed.

nms:t.1890.330.name: Emilie Savage-Smith
nms:t.1890.330.role: Historian and author of the later globe study
nms:t.1890.330.detail: The study’s numbered entry and index give 1890-331 for its no. 27. The museum’s current accession field gives T.1890.330, leaving their exact relationship open.

smg:1901-51.name: J. J. Thomson
smg:1901-51.detail: His series of cathode-ray investigations used apparatus including this original tube. The safe table trial asks which mark moved with a changed condition.

nps:89002457.name: A. B. Crawford
nps:89002457.role: Architect named by the National Register
nps:89002457.detail: The nomination connects Crawford to the Holmdel structure. It gives Project Echo as the original purpose.

nps:89002457.name: Arno Penzias
nps:89002457.detail: Penzias and Wilson published their measurement of excess antenna temperature in July 1965.

nps:89002457.name: Robert Wilson
nps:89002457.detail: Wilson and Penzias checked the receiver and compared directions while tracking a persistent excess.

nps:89002457.name: Robert Dicke
nps:89002457.role: Princeton investigator on the companion explanation
nps:89002457.detail: Dicke’s team supplied a separately argued interpretation of the observed excess.
